newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No brutal 3.0 pct EMU deficit target - de Silguy. [CORRECTED 15:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: No brutal 3.0 pct EMU deficit target - de Silguy. [CORRECTED 15:47 GMT]

text.p: European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Tuesday there was no question of the 3.0 percent deficit qualifying criteria for the single European currency being "brutally" applied.

"It's not a question of applying too brutally simply the figure of three percent," his spokesman, Patrick Child, quoted him as telling Italian journalists during a briefing on the economic situation in France. "It's necessary to look at all of the treaty conditions and the text that surrounds it."
However, at the same time he stressed the need to protect the euro's credibility.
"There is a small margin of manoeuvre but we should not take risks with the credibility of the euro."
Under the EU's Maastricht Treaty, members of the euro zone are supposed to limit government budget deficits to no more than 3.0 percent of GDP.
